events.text:
A Russian military jet landed in Israel Sunday night, and who was on board is still a mystery.
The aircraft is a Tupolev TU-154, used to fly senior officials and military personnel. It took off from Chkalovsky air base near Moscow and touched down at Ben Gurion Airport around 9 p.m. Flight trackers caught it first. It is expected to depart at noon. No comparable flight has landed in Israel in recent years.
IDF contacts with the Russian military have mostly focused on Russian forces in Syria. Russia thinned out its Syria presence after invading Ukraine and recently began moving forces back to a base near Latakia.
5 days ago, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, met Putin in Moscow. The U.S.-Iran campaign was among the topics. Russia is set to supply Iran with Sukhoi Su-35 fighter jets.
IDF and Russian Embassy in Israel: "No response."

events.text:
🇶🇦 Qatar looks to Iran for power lifeline after strikes expose Gulf vulnerabilities 
Qatar is exploring securing a power cable from Iran as a crucial backup amid regional tensions, reports The Cradle.
Talks on connecting the two countries’ power grids began years before the recent US-Israeli war on Iran. 
Retaliatory Iranian missile [strikes](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76289) on Ras Laffan damaged Qatar’s gas facilities and the power-desalination plant that turns turbine heat into drinking water - lending the project new urgency.
🔴 Qatar’s Kahramaa awarded a $1.7M feasibility study contract to Energoprojekt Entel in June 2025
🔴 Iran’s energy minister said in 2026 that the study was nearing completion 
🔴 Qatar and Iran have yet to clarify proposed capacity, financing, electricity trade arrangements & emergency supply commitments
Qatar already has strategic water reservoirs and access to the Gulf Cooperation Council’s shared electricity network via the UAE. An Iranian connection could add another source of electricity.
Iran already has experience with cross-border power deals: it signed an operating agreement with Turkey for the 400-kV Van–Khoy link in 2024, while Pakistan’s 2023 Polan–Gabd line was designed to deliver an additional 100 MW of Iranian electricity. 
Any new deal would need clear rules on electricity volumes, prices and emergency transfers - including how much power Iran can guarantee. 
In 2023, Iran itself faced summer peak electricity demand exceeding available supply by 12 GW.
US sanctions could further complicate payments, insurance and equipment supplies.
Ultimately, the project could turn a long-discussed energy partnership into a practical regional resilience mechanism, argues the publication.

🇺🇸 US evacuates aircraft from UK airbase amid Iranian threat - report
The US has moved several military aircraft, including aerial refueling tankers, from RAF Mildenhall in England to Germany and other locations following a threat from Iran, according to The Wall Street Journal.
🔴 The exact nature of the threat remains unclear, but US officials have raised concerns about possible attacks on American aircraft and personnel
🔴 Security at RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath has been raised to FPCON Charlie, indicating intelligence of a likely terrorist threat
🔴 The move follows the withdrawal of B-1 bombers from another UK base last month amid concerns over an alleged Iranian-backed plot involving drones
🔴 The developments come as Trump weighs further strikes on Iran. However, he said Monday that renewed military action was not currently necessary, citing progress in negotiations
The US president warned that Washington remained ready to act if the situation changed.
